blocks.md: Here is Enbrel (Amgen) against Skyrizi, Rinvoq, Humira on the five rows the case asks for: approved uses, boxed warnings and safety fine print, dosing and convenience, patent and exclusivity timeline, and pricing and gross-to-net exposure. What limits Enbrel's growth is the Medicare negotiated price, worth about $342M a year in the base case, and the market has not clearly priced it in [1][2][3]. Tied finding: Enbrel is an IRA-selected drug whose Medicare negotiated price takes effect 2026-01-01, about $4,751 below the 30-day list price, which puts roughly $342M base ($2M bull to $681M bear) of annual revenue at risk [1][2]. Our call: the market has not clearly priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [4].

memos.summary: Recommend Defend for Amgen: customers are taking longer to pay than revenue growth explains; not priced in: the needle clears the strict obscurity floor.

blocks.md: Template stance, no valued move yet: options are ranked by rules on the verified findings; no budgeted move has been valued for this company.

**Move: Defend.** Fix the exposure the filings reveal (channel, receivables, margin, disclosure) before the market prices it. The verified findings behind it point the same way: customers are taking longer to pay than revenue growth explains, with operating income lower in the base case (impact math below) [1][2]. No budget is valued yet; the commitment is to act on those findings before the next quarterly filing.

blocks.text: Why: the five findings that drive it

blocks.md: The Sharpest Needle (row one below): customers are taking longer to pay than revenue growth explains [3][4]. Impact math, as gated: 0.03 x Rev_TTM 38,095.0 x (1 - t 0.1501) / D 544.0 (operating income lower) [1][5][2]. Why the market has not priced it: not in the earnings-release headline and not asked on calls; qa_turns regex 'receivable': 0 of 10 quarters [6].

rows: Receivables 10,227 vs 8,701 a year earlier (+17.5%, 2026Q2 vs 2025Q2) against quarterly revenue 10,054 vs 9,179 (+9.5%); gap +8.0 pts (derived); peer median -0.3 pts, z +1.2 (derived from the shortlist peer panel, not page-cited) [3][4]
0.03 x Rev_TTM 38,095.0 x (1 - t 0.1501) / D 544.0 (operating income lower) [1][5][2]
Otezla's Medicare price is set by negotiation from January 2027: CMS Part B+D spend $994.0M; base list discount 65% (CMS-published analog, cited) [7][8]

items: **Reprice**: would reset net price and contracting where IRA, MFN or gross-to-net pressure lands. Its findings (medicare price setting reaches this product [7][1][11]) carry less materiality than the needle, so it stays the fallback if the Defend kill signals fire.

**Attack**: would press a label, dosing or safety advantage over rivals with prescribers and payers. Its findings (dosing is less frequent than rivals' [12][2]) carry less materiality than the needle, so it stays the fallback if the Defend kill signals fire.
Receivables growth falls back inside revenue growth in the next two 10-Qs. Baseline: customers are taking longer to pay than revenue growth explains [3][4].
CMS's next selected-drug list or MFP schedule leaves the product's exposure unchanged. Baseline: medicare price setting reaches this product [7][8].
The company's own disclosure puts the Medicaid MFN cost well below this estimate in the next 10-Q. Baseline: the MFN agreement reaches Medicaid [9][10].
Q3 2026 revenue growth lands outside our sealed forecast (80% interval +2.4% to +16.2%), which was hashed and committed before results [17].

blocks.md: Two signals firing in one quarter pause the move and re-run the valuation.

Not priced in: the needle clears the strict obscurity floor. Analysts raised inventory channel in 0 of 10 quarters (tier: never asked) [18]. Who decides its fate: payers: CMS (Medicare negotiation) and Part D plan sponsors; investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

items: Receivables growth falls back inside revenue growth in the next two 10-Qs. Baseline today: Receivables 10,227 vs 8,701 a year earlier (+17.5%, 2026Q2 vs 2025Q2) against quarterly revenue 10,054 vs 9,179 (+9.5%); gap +8.0 pts (derived); peer median -0.3 pts, z +1.2 (derived from the shortlist peer panel, not page-cited) [1][2].

Baseline today: AMGN signed an MFN agreement on 2025-12-19 that extends MFN pricing to Medicaid (R023); TrumpRx: Repatha $573 -> $239/mo (R031). blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Defend commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.

Who decides its fate: Payers: CMS (Medicare negotiation) and Part D plan sponsors; Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

blocks.md: The Reprice move for Gilead Sciences rests on the findings below. Each signal names the filing or data row we will re-read, and the baseline it must move from; if two fire in the same quarter, leadership pauses the move and the valuation is re-run.

items: CMS's next selected-drug list or MFP schedule leaves the product's exposure unchanged. Baseline today: Biktarvy's Medicare price is set by negotiation from January 2028: CMS Part B+D spend $3,904.5M; assumed base list discount 65.5% (median of the cycle 1-2 negotiated discounts in the CMS fact sheets; cited range 38% to 85%; no same-class MFP published) [1][2].

The company's own disclosure puts the Medicaid MFN cost well below this estimate in the next 10-Q. Baseline today: GILD signed an MFN agreement on 2025-12-19 that extends MFN pricing to Medicaid (R025); US investment pledge $32bn; TrumpRx: Epclusa $24,920 -> $2,425 (R033). Direction: adverse to US net price; size not disclosed (deal terms confidential), so no dollar figure is given [3][4].

A new DailyMed label version for the product or a rival closes the gap within twelve months. Baseline today: Biktarvy carries a boxed warning (WARNING: POST TREATMENT ACUTE EXACERBATION OF HEPATITIS B); Cabenuva does not [5][6].
Q3 2026 revenue growth lands outside our sealed forecast (80% interval +3.3% to +12.5%), which was hashed and committed before results [7].

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Reprice commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.

Who decides its fate: Payers: CMS (Medicare negotiation) and Part D plan sponsors; Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

What limits Farxiga's growth is the Medicare negotiated price, worth about $381M a year in the base case, and the market has not clearly priced it in [1][2]. Our call: the market has not clearly priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [3].

blocks.md: Template stance, no valued move yet: options are ranked by rules on the verified findings; no budgeted move has been valued for this company.

**Move: Defend.** Fix the exposure the filings reveal (channel, receivables, margin, disclosure) before the market prices it. The verified findings behind it point the same way: customers are taking longer to pay than revenue growth explains, with operating income lower in the base case (impact math below) [1]. No budget is valued yet; the commitment is to act on those findings before the next quarterly filing.

memos.summary: Keytruda vs Opdivo, Imfinzi, Tecentriq on label, safety, dosing, exclusivity and pricing.

blocks.md: Here is Keytruda (Merck) against Opdivo, Imfinzi, Tecentriq on the five rows the case asks for: approved uses, boxed warnings and safety fine print, dosing and convenience, patent and exclusivity timeline, and pricing and gross-to-net exposure. What limits Keytruda's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $5.35B a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [1][2]. Tied finding: Keytruda loses US exclusivity in 2028, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 28% of peak sales from comparable biologic products, about $5.35B base ($3.94B bull to $11.60B bear) on Keytruda's $18.83B of annual revenue [1][2]. Our call: the market has already priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [3].

memos.summary: Januvia vs Generic sitagliptin, Ozempic, Jardiance on label, safety, dosing, exclusivity and pricing.

blocks.md: Here is Januvia (Merck) against Generic sitagliptin, Ozempic, Jardiance on the five rows the case asks for: approved uses, boxed warnings and safety fine print, dosing and convenience, patent and exclusivity timeline, and pricing and gross-to-net exposure. What limits Januvia's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $880M a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [1]. Tied finding: Januvia loses US exclusivity in 2026, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 88% of peak sales from comparable small molecule products, about $880M base ($747M bull to $923M bear) on Januvia's $999M of annual revenue [1]. Our call: the market has already priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [2].

memos.summary: Recommend Defend for Merck & Co.: gross margin moved sharply; not priced in: the needle clears the strict obscurity floor.

blocks.md: Template stance, no valued move yet: options are ranked by rules on the verified findings; no budgeted move has been valued for this company.

**Move: Defend.** Fix the exposure the filings reveal (channel, receivables, margin, disclosure) before the market prices it. The verified findings behind it point the same way: gross margin moved sharply, with operating income lower in the base case (impact math below) [1][2]. No budget is valued yet; the commitment is to act on those findings before the next quarterly filing.

blocks.text: Why: the five findings that drive it

blocks.md: The Sharpest Needle (row one below): gross margin moved sharply [3][4]. Impact math, as gated: 0.03 x Rev_TTM 66,569.0 x (1 - t 0.1854) / D 2,470.0 (operating income lower) [1][5][2]. Why the market has not priced it: not in the earnings-release headline and not asked on calls; qa_turns regex 'gross margin|cost of (sales|products)': 0 of 10 quarters [6].

items: **Attack**: would press a label, dosing or safety advantage over rivals with prescribers and payers. Its findings (a rival carries a boxed warning it does not [9][2]) carry less materiality than the needle, so it stays the fallback if the Defend kill signals fire.

**Reprice**: would reset net price and contracting where IRA, MFN or gross-to-net pressure lands. Its findings (the filing wording changed [16][2]) carry less materiality than the needle, so it stays the fallback if the Defend kill signals fire.
Gross margin holds at the prior-year level in the next two quarterly reports. Baseline: gross margin moved sharply [3][4].
CMS's next selected-drug list or MFP schedule leaves the product's exposure unchanged. Baseline: medicare price setting reaches this product [7][8].
A new DailyMed label version for the product or a rival closes the gap within twelve months. Baseline: a rival carries a boxed warning it does not [9][10].
Q3 2026 revenue growth lands outside our sealed forecast (80% interval -0.5% to +10.2%), which was hashed and committed before results [17].

blocks.md: Two signals firing in one quarter pause the move and re-run the valuation.

Not priced in: the needle clears the strict obscurity floor. Who decides its fate: investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

items: Gross margin holds at the prior-year level in the next two quarterly reports. Baseline today: Gross margin 73.5% vs 77.5% a year earlier (-4.0 pts) (Q2 2026); peer median 74.1%, z -0.1 [1][2].

Q3 2026 revenue growth lands outside our sealed forecast (80% interval -0.5% to +10.2%), which was hashed and committed before results [7].

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Defend commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.
Who decides its fate: Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

 The nine manufacturers include Amgen, Bristol Myers Squibb, Boehringer Ingelheim, Genentech, Gilead Sciences, GSK, Merck, Novartis, and Sanofi.

blocks.md: Here is Wegovy (Novo Nordisk) against Mounjaro, Zepbound, Foundayo on the five rows the case asks for: approved uses, boxed warnings and safety fine print, dosing and convenience, patent and exclusivity timeline, and pricing and gross-to-net exposure. What limits Wegovy's growth is the Medicare negotiated price, worth about $28M a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [1][2][3]. Tied finding: Wegovy is an IRA-selected drug whose Medicare negotiated price takes effect 2027-01-01, about $685 below the 30-day list price, which puts roughly $28M base ($3M bull to $52M bear) of annual revenue at risk [1][2]. Our call: the market has already priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [4].

blocks.md: The Defend move for Novo Nordisk rests on the findings below. Each signal names the filing or data row we will re-read, and the baseline it must move from; if two fire in the same quarter, leadership pauses the move and the valuation is re-run.

items: Gross margin holds at the prior-year level in the next two quarterly reports. Baseline today: Gross margin 81.0% vs 84.7% a year earlier (-3.7 pts) (FY2025); peer median 74.1%, z +1.1 [1][2].

Inventory days fall back toward the peer median in the next two 10-Qs. Baseline today: Inventory 49,623 vs 40,849 a year earlier (+21.5%, 2025 vs 2024) against annual revenue 309,064 vs 290,403 (+6.4%); gap +15.1 pts (derived); peer median -4.5 pts, z +1.3 (derived from the shortlist peer panel, not page-cited) [3][1].

CMS's next selected-drug list or MFP schedule leaves the product's exposure unchanged. Baseline today: Ozempic/Rybelsus/Wegovy's Medicare price is set by negotiation from January 2027: CMS Part B+D spend $14,426.6M; base list discount 71% (CMS-published analog, cited) [4][5].
Gross margin holds at the prior-year level in the next two quarterly reports.

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Defend commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.
Who decides its fate: Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

What limits Zepbound's growth is the shift of volume to the lower cash price, worth about $3.14B a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [1][2]. Tied finding: The US cash price of $346 a month sits 68% below Zepbound's $1,086 list price, so every point of volume that moves to the cash channel gives up net revenue; on an assumed 10 to 40 percent of volume the range is $3.14B base ($1.26B bull to $5.02B bear) [1][2]. blocks.md: Here is Trulicity (Eli Lilly) against Ozempic, Wegovy injection, Wegovy pill on the five rows the case asks for: approved uses, boxed warnings and safety fine print, dosing and convenience, patent and exclusivity timeline, and pricing and gross-to-net exposure. What limits Trulicity's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $1.76B a year in the base case, and the market has not clearly priced it in [1][2]. Tied finding: Trulicity loses US exclusivity in 2027, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 28% of peak sales from comparable biologic products, about $1.76B base ($1.30B bull to $3.82B bear) on Trulicity's $6.20B of annual revenue [1][2]. Our call: the market has not clearly priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [3].

blocks.text: Kill signals, first six to twelve months

blocks.md: The Reprice move for Eli Lilly rests on the findings below. Each signal names the filing or data row we will re-read, and the baseline it must move from; if two fire in the same quarter, leadership pauses the move and the valuation is re-run.

items: CMS's next selected-drug list or MFP schedule leaves the product's exposure unchanged. Baseline today: Trulicity's Medicare price is set by negotiation from January 2028: CMS Part B+D spend $4,898.4M; base list discount 71% (CMS-published analog, cited) [1][2].

The company's own disclosure puts the Medicaid MFN cost well below this estimate in the next 10-Q. Baseline today: LLY signed an MFN agreement on 2025-11-06 that extends MFN pricing to Medicaid (R010); US investment pledge $50bn; TrumpRx: Zepbound avg $346/mo; Trulicity $389/mo (R012). Direction: adverse to US net price; size not disclosed (deal terms confidential), so no dollar figure is given [3][4].
R&D share of revenue returns toward the peer median in the next two 10-Qs. Baseline today: R&D 16.6% of revenue vs 21.4% a year earlier (-4.8 pts) (Q2 2026); peer median 18.6%, z -0.3 [5][6].
Q3 2026 revenue growth lands outside our sealed forecast (80% interval +29.7% to +67.9%), which was hashed and committed before results [7].

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Reprice commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.

Who decides its fate: Payers: CMS (Medicare negotiation) and Part D plan sponsors; Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

Our call: the market has already priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [2].

memos.prompt: How does NEEDLE work?
memos.summary: Detect, verify to the page, score, gate, seal: the pipeline in plain words.

blocks.md: **Detect.** Rule-based detectors read every filing, call and label in the corpus and flag candidates: inventory or receivables outrunning revenue, margin and tax swings, wording drift, deflected questions, label gaps, the three policy forces. **Verify.** A finding survives only if its quote is on the cited page and every figure is found there or derived from figures that are; the rest go to a rejected log (271 rows so far [1]). **Score.** S = M x O x E x pi: earnings at risk, times how little the market discusses it, times evidence quality, times the backtested chance it matters; the league ranks each company on its top five. **Gate.** Every sentence here passed a per-number citation gate; failed rows are excluded, oversized impacts withheld. **Seal.** Revenue forecasts for 7 companies were hashed (sha256) and committed before Q3 results [2]. Calibrated on 1793 firm-quarters, the forecaster's interval covered 0.794 against a 0.8 target [3]; a blind test on J&J's Q3 release landed inside it [4]. **Ledger.** Every run appends to a hash-chained ledger (110 records, intact at export [5]). **Honesty.** The CEO memo is drafted by rules from verified findings, not by a model, and says so.
